Simulate tag transmissions along tracks

simulate_transmissions.Rd

Places the transmissions of a tag with a random delay along each simulated track. tag_delay is defined as in detfield::bin_detections(): the time from the start of one transmission to the start of the next, the transmission itself included. Each interval is drawn uniformly between the shortest and the longest delay, as in the transmission model of glatos::transmit_along_path(), and the first transmission falls at a uniform random time within the first interval. The transmissions do not depend on the step of the walk: a tag with a 120 s mean delay sends 3600 / 120 = 30 transmissions an hour whatever the time step, the n that detfield::bin_detections() gives for the same tag_delay. Each transmission's position is interpolated along the straight step that holds it, so it lies on water.

Usage

simulate_transmissions(tracks, tag_delay = c(65, 185), seed = NULL)

Arguments

tracks

A sim_tracks object from simulate_tracks().

tag_delay

Delay from the start of one transmission to the start of the next, in seconds: one number for a fixed delay, or two, the shortest and the longest, both above 0.

seed

Seed; NULL uses the current random number stream. The caller's stream is restored after a seeded call. The draws depend on the generator kind as well as the seed; the kind is stored with the result.

Value

A data frame of class sim_transmissions, one row per transmission, ordered by path and time: transmission_id (integer), path_id, animal_id (the path as character), transmitter

("SIM-0001", ...), datetime (POSIXct, UTC), x, y, cell, state, and min_delay and max_delay, the delay range used, in seconds, under the suite's column names (transmitter, min_delay, max_delay, as detfield::bin_detections() reads them), so unique(tx[c("transmitter", "min_delay", "max_delay")]) is a tag_delay

table for detfield::bin_detections(). Attributes: tag_delay (the two numbers), seed, rng_kind (the RNGkind() in force), and epsg and grid, taken from the tracks.

Details

A tag sheet usually gives the programmed delay without the transmission, a few seconds: add it. The default, 65 to 185 s, is a tag programmed at 60 to 180 s with a 5 s transmission, 28.8 transmissions an hour.

See also

simulate_tracks(), simulate_detections()

Examples

stoney <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif",
                                  package = "arraydesign"))
# Two animals for 2 hours.
walk <- crw_model(30, 15, 40, time_step_s = 60)
tr <- simulate_tracks(stoney, walk, n_animals = 2, n_steps = 120, seed = 1)
tx <- simulate_transmissions(tr, tag_delay = c(120, 180), seed = 2)
head(tx)
#>   transmission_id path_id animal_id transmitter            datetime
#> 1               1       1         1    SIM-0001 2025-01-01 00:01:56
#> 2               2       1         1    SIM-0001 2025-01-01 00:04:38
#> 3               3       1         1    SIM-0001 2025-01-01 00:07:12
#> 4               4       1         1    SIM-0001 2025-01-01 00:09:22
#> 5               5       1         1    SIM-0001 2025-01-01 00:12:19
#> 6               6       1         1    SIM-0001 2025-01-01 00:15:16
#>          x       y cell state min_delay max_delay
#> 1 735001.9 4939666 3843     1       120       180
#> 2 735057.6 4939755 3676     1       120       180
#> 3 735098.6 4939811 3676     1       120       180
#> 4 735069.2 4939800 3676     1       120       180
#> 5 735063.7 4939736 3844     1       120       180
#> 6 735055.0 4939650 3844     1       120       180
# Transmissions per hour of track: about 3600 / 150 = 24.
nrow(tx) / (2 * 120 * 60 / 3600)
#> [1] 24.25
